feedback: Written before this robot has raced. Evidence from iteration 0: all 60 trials ended off track with 0 finishes. Mean progress was 0.10 to 0.14, max_error reached about 0.061 m, and RMS error was small (0.024 to 0.030 m). That pattern means the robot tracks well until it suddenly drifts off at the edge of a bend, so the problem is edge loss, not general tracking error. The Integrator had to make three compensations for this geometry. First, the sensor spread is wider (±0.05 m), so the 0.025 m spacing gives a graded signal at larger lateral error, and the antisymmetric weights [-2,-1,0,1,2] still work. Second, the narrower wheel_track (0.10 m) increases yaw per unit of wheel differential, so kp was lowered from 3.0 to 2.5 to avoid over-steering. Third, the lighter body and shorter lead reduce yaw inertia and lag, so kd was raised to 0.30 for damping. Changes to try next, depending on the next race: (1) If max_error is still above 0.06 m on the oval or s-bend and line_loss_events is above 0, try sensor_size 0.016 with the same x positions, to widen the capture band at the edge. (2) If steering_oscillation is high (above about 0.15) while rms_error is low, reduce wheel_track narrowing: try wheel_track 0.12 m to lower turn authority, or raise sensor y lead to 0.04 m to reduce control lag. (3) If the robot tracks cleanly but mean progress stays low, the limit is probably drivetrain speed, so try wheel_radius 0.04 m to increase ground speed for the same PWM.
requested_changes: If max_error reaches 0.06 m or line_loss_events > 0 on the oval or s-bend, set sensor_size to 0.016 (from 0.012) with the same x and y positions, because the iteration 0 edge loss (max_error 0.061 m, 1 line loss per run) suggests the sensors lose the tape too early.

If steering_oscillation is above about 0.15 while rms_error is below 0.03 m, set wheel_track to 0.12 m (from 0.10 m) and keep sensor y at 0.03 m, because the narrower track raised turn authority and iteration 0 showed higher oscillation on the slalom (0.137) than on the oval (0.085).

If the robot completes with low max_error but mean progress stays below 0.5, set wheel_radius to 0.04 m (from 0.035 m), because the 3.0 s limit needs about 1.5 m/s average speed and iteration 0 showed the drivetrain, not tracking, limited progress on the slalom (progress 0.10).
